question: The triad of group 2 metals consists of which of the following elements?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ca, Sr, Ba.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Group 2 metals **are also known as **alkaline earth metals** and are located in the **second column **of the periodic table.
 
• The triad of group 2 metals is a group of **three elements** that have** similar properties** and are located in the same row of the periodic table.
 
• The triad of group 2 metals consists of the elements with atomic numbers **12 (Ca), 38 (Sr), and 56 (Ba).**
 
• These elements are al**l metals,** have a** shiny appearance**, and are reactive with water and acids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sulfur (S), nitrogen (N), and oxygen (O) are **nonmetals** and are located in th**e p-block** of the periodic table.
 
• Carbon (C) is a** nonmetal **and is located in the** p-block** of the periodic table.
 
• Copper (Cu) is a **transition metal **and is located in the **d-block **of the periodic table.
 
• Fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), and iodine (I) are **halogens** and have different physical and chemical properties than the group 2 metals.
